content: Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When this product is expired or no longer needed, dispose of it properly. The information provided here was last updated in June 2024. Important Usage Information: This document is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. How to Use: Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically four times a day (every six hours). Ampicillin should be taken on an empty stomach, either one hour before or two hours after a meal, with a full glass of water. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or mouth/tongue sores. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions are rare, but ampicillin can commonly cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before taking ampicillin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, penicillin, cephalosporin antibiotics, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ampicillin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Ampicillin passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Ampicillin may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Additional Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. If you are using this drug for an extended period, lab and/or medical tests (such as kidney/liver function and complete blood count) should be performed regularly. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and personalized information.
